transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I came in because I just... I can’t seem to get out from under this really heavy, hopeless feeling. It’s like everything I tried to rebuild after my divorce — my life, my sense of stability, just the idea that I was going to be okay — it feels like it all collapsed at once, and I’m just sitting underneath it.

I know that sounds dramatic, but that’s honestly what it feels like. I keep trying to tell myself I’ve handled hard things before, I’m an engineer, I’m supposed to be practical and solve problems, but this doesn’t feel like a problem I can solve. It feels like I’m buried in it. That’s why I’m here.
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these feelings been continuous over the past couple of weeks, or have they come and gone?

It’s been about a month now, I think. Not just a bad day here and there — it’s been sort of hanging over me most of the time since the financial mess after the divorce really hit. I keep trying to pinpoint the exact day it started, but it’s more like things piled up and then suddenly I realized I wasn’t coming back up for air.

Over the past few weeks it’s felt pretty continuous. There might be moments where I’m distracted for a little while, but the feeling is still there underneath everything, like it’s waiting for me as soon as I stop moving or stop trying to handle the next thing.
Have you ever felt this way before, or is this the first time you’ve experienced a period of feeling this hopeless and overwhelmed?

I don’t think this is the first time I’ve felt low, exactly, but this particular kind of hopelessness… this feels different in how heavy it is. I’ve had hard periods before, especially around the divorce, where I felt sad or lost or like I didn’t know what my life was supposed to look like anymore. But what I’m feeling now is more like I can’t shake it at all.

It’s like everything I thought I was rebuilding after the divorce — my stability, my plans, just the idea that I was going to land on my feet — collapsed, and I’m just sitting under the wreckage of it. I keep trying to reason my way out of it, like if I can organize the problem then maybe I can fix how I feel, but the hopeless feeling just stays there. So no, not the first time I’ve struggled, but it’s the first time it’s felt this overwhelming and inescapable.
Was there a specific event or situation, aside from the divorce itself, that seemed to trigger or worsen how you’ve been feeling lately?

Yes… I think it was the financial mess after the divorce, more than the divorce itself at this point. The divorce was obviously painful, and it shook up everything, but lately it’s been the money situation that seemed to really knock me down.

It’s been about a month of this feeling hanging over me, and I can trace it pretty closely to when the financial reality started becoming unavoidable — like the bills, the splitting things up, realizing what I could and couldn’t afford, and just feeling like the life I was trying to rebuild wasn’t as stable as I thought. It wasn’t one single dramatic moment exactly, more like a series of things that made me feel trapped and like I couldn’t get ahead.

So yes, I’d say that’s what worsened it. The divorce started the upheaval, but the financial aftermath is what made this past month feel so heavy.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you normally like doing?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, honestly. I mean… I haven’t really been paying attention to pleasure in that way. Lately everything has been so focused on just dealing with what has to be dealt with that I don’t know if I’ve lost interest in things, or if I just haven’t had the space in my head to do them.

There are things I normally like, or at least things that usually feel like “me,” but I haven’t really been stopping to check whether I still enjoy them. It’s more like I keep thinking, okay, once I get through this next bill or this next conversation or this next practical problem, then maybe I’ll feel normal again. So I guess I don’t have a clear answer. I haven’t noticed it in a neat way, like “I used to love this and now I don’t.” It’s more that everything feels kind of crowded out right now.
Can you think back to a time before this heavy feeling started — were you able to enjoy or take pleasure in things back then, and how does that compare to how you feel about those things now?

I’m trying to think back and it’s honestly a little blurry, not because it was that long ago, but because everything now kind of colors how I remember it. Before this got so heavy, I think I was still capable of enjoying things, at least in moments. Like if something was pleasant, I could recognize it as pleasant, if that makes sense. I could get absorbed in normal life a bit more.

Now… I don’t know if I’d say I feel nothing toward those things, exactly. It’s more like I don’t even reach for them the same way. Or if I think about doing something I used to like, it feels like there’s this extra layer between me and it, like I’d have to push through so much mental weight just to get there. And then I start thinking, “What’s the point, I have all this other stuff hanging over me,” and I don’t really get far enough to find out whether I’d enjoy it.

So I can’t give you a clean before-and-after answer like, “Yes, I loved things then and now I don’t.” I think before, enjoyment was more available to me. Now it feels distant, or crowded out, or like something I’m supposed to be able to access but can’t quite get to.
Looking back, would you say that you’re no longer able to feel pleasure or interest in things you used to enjoy, even when you make time for them?

I don’t know that I can say that clearly. Like, “no longer able” feels very definite, and I’m not sure I’ve actually tested it in a fair way.

If I make time for something, I’m usually not really… present for it, I guess. I might sit there with the intention of doing something normal or something I used to like, but my mind keeps circling back to everything else, and then it’s hard to tell if I’m not enjoying the thing, or if I’m just too preoccupied to let myself enjoy it. It’s like I’m physically doing it, but mentally I’m still somewhere else.

So I wouldn’t want to say I’m completely unable to feel pleasure. That sounds stronger than what I know for sure. I just know it doesn’t come easily right now, and I don’t reach for things the way I used to. Even when there is time, it doesn’t feel like real time, if that makes sense — it feels borrowed or guilty or like I should be handling something more urgent. So maybe the interest is still there somewhere, but it’s buried under all of that.
Even when you’re not thinking about the financial issues or other stressors, do you still find yourself unable to enjoy or feel interested in activities that you used to like?

I’m not sure I can separate it that cleanly, honestly. Like, I get what you’re asking — whether even in a quiet moment, with nothing actively pressing on me, I still can’t enjoy things — but I don’t know that I really have many moments that feel separate from all of it.

Even if I’m not consciously thinking, “the finances” or “this problem” or “that problem,” there’s still this background feeling, like a hum. So if I sit down to do something I used to like, I might not be actively worrying in words, but I’m also not exactly relaxed or open to enjoying it. And then I start judging myself for not enjoying it, which probably makes it worse.

So… I don’t know. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern where I’m completely free of stress and still definitely unable to enjoy anything. It’s more that I can’t really tell what I would feel if all that noise actually went quiet. Right now it all blends together.
Even when you’re not preoccupied with stress or financial worries, do you find that you have less interest or pleasure in activities than you used to, even if just doing them briefly?

I still don’t know how to answer that in a clean yes-or-no way. I’m sorry, I know you’re asking it very specifically and I keep kind of circling around it, but that’s honestly how it feels in my head.

If I do something briefly — like even just starting something I used to like — I can tell that I’m not as pulled toward it as I remember being. But I don’t know if that means the interest or pleasure itself is gone, or if I’m just not settling into it long enough for anything to happen. Sometimes I’ll start and almost immediately feel like, “This isn’t working,” but I’m also watching myself the whole time, like I’m checking whether I’m enjoying it, which probably makes it impossible to enjoy it normally.

And even when I’m not actively thinking about money or stress, I don’t feel like there’s some neutral version of me sitting there calmly trying the activity. It’s more like I’m still tense underneath, or disconnected, or distracted in a way I don’t always have words for. So I haven’t really noticed, “Oh, even with no worries, I definitely get no pleasure from anything.” I can’t honestly say that. What I can say is that things don’t feel easy or inviting the way they used to, and I don’t trust my own read on whether that’s because I’ve lost interest or because everything in me is just… not available right now.
Can you think of a time recently when you weren’t thinking about your stress or worries, and if so, did you notice if your usual activities still felt interesting or enjoyable then?

I’m trying to think of one, and I’m honestly having trouble coming up with a clean example. Not because I’m never doing anything other than worrying, exactly, but because when I look back on it, I can’t tell what was going on in my head with enough confidence.

Like, there might be a moment where I’m making coffee or scrolling through something or half-watching a show, and I’m not actively thinking, “Here is the thing I’m stressed about.” But I don’t know if that counts as not thinking about it, because I still feel kind of… loaded, if that makes sense. Like my mind is quiet on the surface, but I’m not relaxed.

And in those moments, I don’t really know that I test enjoyment properly. I’m either distracted, or I notice myself checking, “Am I enjoying this? Does this feel normal?” And then the checking kind of ruins the answer. So I can’t honestly say, “Yes, I had a stress-free moment and even then nothing felt good,” but I also can’t say, “No, everything feels enjoyable when I’m not worried.” I just don’t have a clear recent example where the worries were gone enough for me to know.
Can you think of a time recently when you were fully engaged in an activity without thinking about your stress or worries, and if so, did that activity feel interesting or enjoyable to you then?

I wish I could give you a clearer example, but I really can’t think of a recent time where I was fully engaged like that — like absorbed enough in something that the worries dropped away and I could then tell you, “Yes, this was enjoyable,” or “No, it wasn’t.”

There are times I’m doing an activity, but I don’t know if I’d call it engaged. I might be physically doing it, or going through the motions, or kind of half-paying attention, but there’s still this part of me monitoring myself or waiting for the stress to come back into focus. And then once I notice I’m trying to figure out whether I’m enjoying it, it becomes weirdly impossible to answer.

So… no, I can’t really identify a moment like that recently. Not in a clean way. I’m not saying it definitely never happens, but if it does, I’m not noticing it clearly enough to tell you what it felt like.
Would you say that your mood has been consistently low throughout most of the day, nearly every day, even when there’s no specific stressor actively on your mind?

Yes… I think yes. Not in a neat, dramatic way every single minute, but most of the day there’s this heaviness sitting on me. Even when I’m not actively thinking about a specific bill or work thing or whatever, it’s still there.

That’s actually why I came in. I can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling, like everything I managed to build for myself after the divorce has just collapsed somehow, and I’m sitting underneath it. It’s not always tied to one thought in the moment. Sometimes I’ll realize I’m not even thinking about anything specific, but my mood is still down, like the bottom has dropped out and I’m just carrying that around.

So… yes, it feels pretty constant lately. Even when there isn’t one obvious stressor in front of me, I don’t feel okay.
Even when you’re not focused on the financial issues or other stressors, do you find that activities you used to enjoy don’t bring you any pleasure at all anymore?

I’m not completely sure how to answer “no pleasure at all,” because that sounds very absolute, and I don’t know if I can measure it that cleanly.

What I can say is that things don’t seem to land the way they used to. Like, if I put on something I normally like, or try to do something that should feel relaxing, I’m often aware that I’m not really getting much from it. But then I start second-guessing myself — am I not enjoying it because I’m still tense in the background, even if I’m not actively thinking about money or some specific problem? Or am I genuinely just not enjoying it anymore? I don’t know.

I haven’t really had many moments lately where I feel clear enough to say, “Okay, the stress is fully out of the picture, and this activity still feels empty.” It’s more like everything is kind of muted, and I’m there, but I’m not sure whether that’s lack of pleasure or just being weighed down in general. So I wouldn’t want to say “no pleasure at all” with confidence. I just know it doesn’t feel normal.
Can you think of a recent time when you were doing something you used to genuinely enjoy, and even if just for a short while, you felt a clear sense of pleasure or interest in it?

I’m trying to think of one, and honestly… nothing comes to mind clearly. I wish I could point to something simple, like “I watched a show I like and laughed,” or “I got into a project for twenty minutes,” but when I scan back over the last little while it all feels kind of blurred.

There are things I used to enjoy, sure, but recently when I’ve done them, I can’t say I felt a clear little spark of pleasure or interest. Sometimes I keep doing something because it’s familiar, or because I think maybe it will help if I just stick with it long enough, but I’m mostly aware of trying to get through the time. And then I start analyzing it while I’m doing it, like, “Am I enjoying this? Is this helping? Shouldn’t this feel good?” which sort of ruins any chance of just naturally enjoying it.

So… no, I can’t give you a solid recent example. Maybe there have been tiny moments I didn’t register, but if you’re asking for a clear sense of pleasure or interest, even briefly, I don’t really remember one.
Have you noticed that you feel more tired or that you have less energy than usual, even when you’re not doing much physically?

Yes. Very much, actually. It’s not even just “I’m a little tired” in the normal sense, like after a long day or after doing something physical. It feels like everything takes this huge amount of effort that it shouldn’t take.

Getting through a normal workday feels like dragging wet concrete. That’s the best way I can describe it. I’ll be sitting there trying to do things I know how to do, things I’ve done for years, and it feels like I’m moving through this thick resistance. Even opening my laptop can feel like a task before the actual task. I’ll look at it and think, okay, just open it, just start, and somehow that alone feels like more energy than I have.

And it’s the same with basic things, too. Taking a shower, getting dressed, making myself start the day — those feel weirdly heavy. Not complicated, exactly, but like my body and mind are both saying, “No, that’s too much.” Even when I haven’t physically done much, I still feel worn out. It’s like I’m exhausted before I even begin.
Have you found that you no longer look forward to or care about things you used to enjoy, even when you’re not actively thinking about your current stressors?

I think… I’m still not sure how to separate those things cleanly. Like, I can say I don’t really look forward to much lately, but the “even when I’m not actively thinking about stressors” part is hard, because I don’t know that I’m ever fully not carrying them somewhere in the background.

It’s not like I’m sitting there every second thinking, “money, work, problems,” or whatever, but there’s this kind of constant heaviness that follows me around. So when I think about something I used to enjoy, I don’t really get that anticipatory feeling, like, “Oh, that’ll be nice,” or “I’m excited to do that.” It’s more like I think, “Maybe I should do that because it used to help,” but I don’t feel much pull toward it.

And I don’t know if that means I don’t care about those things anymore, exactly. I don’t want to say I don’t care, because part of me cares that I don’t care, if that makes sense. I remember caring. I remember what it felt like to look forward to things. But right now it’s more like I’m going through the motions of trying to access that feeling, and it just doesn’t really show up.

So… yes, in practice I’m not really looking forward to things the way I used to. But I’m hesitant to say it’s completely separate from stress, because I can’t tell where one ends and the other begins.

Looking back, can you recall a time in the past few weeks when you were not preoccupied with stress or worries, and you engaged in an activity you used to enjoy — did you feel any sense of pleasure or interest in that moment, even briefly?

I’m honestly struggling to find a clean example of that. I know you’re trying to separate out the stress piece, like, “Was there a moment where the worries weren’t front and center, and did something still feel enjoyable?” And I get why you’re asking it that way, but when I try to look back over the past few weeks, it’s hard for me to identify a time when I was clearly not preoccupied.

There may have been moments where I wasn’t actively thinking in words about stress, if that makes sense. Like I might have had something on in the background, or tried to do something familiar that I used to like, and I wasn’t specifically sitting there listing my worries. But I still didn’t really feel… free of it. It’s more like the stress is quiet sometimes, but still in the room.

And when I did those kinds of activities, I don’t remember feeling a definite pleasure or interest. Not even in a way where I can say, “Oh yes, for five minutes I was into that.” Mostly I remember monitoring myself while doing it, wondering whether I was enjoying it, or noticing that I wasn’t reacting the way I normally would have. It becomes this weird internal checking process instead of actually being absorbed in anything.

So I guess my answer is: I can’t recall a specific time like that. If there were brief moments, they didn’t stand out enough for me to remember them as pleasure or interest. Right now it mostly feels like I’m trying to do the things that used to mean something to me, but I’m not getting much back from them.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt that nothing — even things you used to really enjoy — could give you even a little pleasure or satisfaction, even for a short time?

I’m not sure I can say it that absolutely — like “nothing” could give me even a little pleasure. That feels hard to answer because I’m not always clear on whether something is pleasure or just… relief that I made it through something, or distraction, or habit.

Over the past couple weeks, I haven’t really had that normal feeling of satisfaction from things I used to enjoy, at least not in a way that stands out. But if you’re asking whether there was literally no tiny moment of anything good at all, I don’t know. I feel hesitant to say that, because maybe there were little flickers that I’m not remembering, or maybe I’m judging them too harshly because they didn’t feel like they used to.

Mostly it’s like things don’t land. I can do something that used to make me feel better, and instead of feeling pleased or interested, I’m kind of waiting to see if it will work. And then when it doesn’t really do much, I feel disappointed, but even that is muted. So… I guess I’d say I haven’t noticed much pleasure or satisfaction, but I’m not completely sure I can say nothing could give me even a little.
